grammar.title: Present simple vs present continuous
grammar.summary: Use the present simple for habits, routines and things that are always or generally true. Use the present continuous for actions happening now and for temporary situations around now.
grammar.summaryMn: Present simple-ийг дадал, давтагддаг үйл, байнга үнэн зүйлд хэрэглэнэ. Present continuous-ийг яг одоо болж буй үйл болон түр зуурын нөхцөл байдалд хэрэглэнэ.
structure: Present simple: I/you/we/they work · he/she/it works · Do you work? · She doesn't work.
Present continuous: am/is/are + verb-ing · I'm working · Are you working? · He isn't working.

usage.example: I usually get up at seven.

usage.use: Actions happening at the moment of speaking
usage.example: Sorry, I can't talk — I'm cooking.
I'm staying with my aunt this month.

examples.note: Permanent job (present simple) vs temporary arrangement (present continuous).

examples.en: She doesn't usually drink coffee, but she's drinking one now because she's tired.
examples.note: General habit vs this particular moment.

examples.en: How often do you go to the gym?
examples.note: Questions about frequency use the present simple.

examples.en: Prices are going up every month.
examples.note: A changing situation uses the present continuous.

pairs.b: I'm living with friends until I find my own flat.
pairs.why: The first sentence is permanent. The second is temporary — it will end soon.
pairs.whyMn: Эхнийх нь байнгын, хоёр дахь нь түр зуурын нөхцөл.

pairs.why: A regular habit vs an action in progress at this moment.
pairs.whyMn: Тогтмол дадал ба яг одоо болж буй үйл.

pairs.why: 'What do you do?' asks about someone's job. 'What are you doing?' asks about this moment.

grammar.title: State verbs
grammar.summary: Some verbs describe states — thoughts, feelings, possession and the senses — not actions. We don't normally use them in the continuous form, even when we talk about now.
grammar.summaryMn: Зарим үйл үг үйлдэл биш, байдал (бодол, мэдрэмж, эзэмшил) илэрхийлдэг. Эдгээрийг одоо тухай ярьж байсан ч ихэвчлэн үргэлжилсэн (-ing) хэлбэрээр хэрэглэдэггүй.
structure: Thinking: know, believe, understand, remember, mean
Feelings: like, love, hate, want, need, prefer
Other states: seem, look like, cost, contain, depend

usage.example: She needs a break right now.

usage.use: Some verbs have an action meaning too

pronunciation.title: Third-person -s: /s/, /z/ and /ɪz/
pronunciation.explanation: The -s ending of verbs (works, plays, watches) has three different sounds. After voiceless sounds like /p/, /t/, /k/, /f/ it sounds like /s/. After voiced sounds and vowels it sounds like /z/. After s, z, sh, ch and j sounds it becomes /ɪz/ — an extra syllable.
pronunciation.explanationMn: Үйл үгийн -s төгсгөл гурван янзаар дуудагдана: хүнгэн гийгүүлэгчийн (/p/, /t/, /k/, /f/) дараа /s/; хөндий гийгүүлэгч, эгшгийн дараа /z/; s, z, sh, ch, j авианы дараа /ɪz/ буюу нэмэлт үе болно.

items.tip: A buzzing sound at the end.

reading.title: Are You a Lark or an Owl?
text: Some people jump out of bed at six o'clock, full of energy. Others press the snooze button three times and still arrive at work half asleep. Scientists call these two groups 'larks' and 'owls', and they say the difference is not just about willpower.

Our body has an internal clock that controls when we feel sleepy and when we feel alert. In larks, this clock runs a little early, so they usually feel their best in the morning. In owls, it runs later, so they often feel most productive in the evening. Most people, in fact, are somewhere in the middle.

The problem is that school and office schedules are usually designed for larks. An owl who has to start work at eight often feels exhausted and may make more mistakes in the morning. Some companies are now changing their routines: they let employees choose their own working hours, as long as they finish their tasks on time.

Can an owl become a lark? Experts say you can move your body clock a little. Getting bright light early in the day, keeping a regular schedule at weekends and avoiding screens late at night all help. But you probably can't change your nature completely — so if you are an owl, it might be better to plan your most difficult tasks for the afternoon.

listening.title: Who does the washing-up?
listening.context: Anna and Tom share a flat with a third student, Mia. Anna wants to talk about the housework.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text: Tom, have you got a minute? I think we need to talk about the flat.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text: Well, the kitchen is a mess again. I did the washing-up on Monday and on Wednesday, and nobody else did it this week.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Oh, sorry. I'm working late every day this month, so I usually get home after ten.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text: I know you're busy. But maybe we can make a schedule and take turns?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That's fair. What about the laundry and the rubbish?

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text: How about this: I do the washing-up on weekdays, you vacuum the living room on Saturdays, and we take turns with the rubbish.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Sounds good. And what about Mia? She hardly ever does anything.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text: She's staying with her parents at the moment, so she isn't here. When she comes back, we can add her to the schedule.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: OK. Can you remind me on Saturday morning? I sometimes forget.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text: Of course. I'll put the schedule on the fridge.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Great. Thanks, Anna — and sorry about the mess.

reading.title: My Upside-Down Day
text: Most people start their day with breakfast. I start mine with dinner. I'm a nurse, and for the last two years I've worked night shifts at a children's hospital. My shift starts at eight in the evening and finishes at eight in the morning.

When I get home, the rest of my family is leaving for work and school. I have a light meal, put on an eye mask and try to sleep until about three in the afternoon. My flatmate is very kind — she never vacuums or plays music while I'm asleep.

The hardest part is my days off. My body doesn't know if it's day or night, and I often feel exhausted. Some nurses keep a night schedule on their days off too, but I prefer to see my friends during normal hours, so I try to change my routine quickly.

At the moment I'm taking an online course in child nutrition, so my spare time is even shorter than usual. But I really love my job. The hospital is quiet at night, and I have time to talk to the children when they can't sleep.

writing.prompt: Write a short blog post (100–130 words) called 'My weekdays and my weekends'. Describe your usual weekday routine, how your weekends are different, and one thing you are doing differently these days.
writing.promptMn: 'Миний ажлын өдрүүд ба амралтын өдрүүд' нэртэй богино блог бичээрэй (100–130 үг).
points: Weekday routine (present simple, adverbs of frequency)
writing.sample: On weekdays my routine is simple. I get up at half past six, have a quick breakfast and commute to work by bus. I usually work until six, and in the evening I often cook dinner and do a few chores. I rarely go out because I'm tired. At weekends, however, everything is slower. I sleep in on Saturdays, run errands in the afternoon and meet friends in the evening. On Sundays I tidy the flat and plan the next week. These days my routine is a little different: I'm learning to drive, so I'm spending most of my spare time on driving lessons. It's hard work, but I'm enjoying it.

speaking.prompt: Talk about a habit you would like to change. Say what you do now, why you want to change it, and what you are doing to change it.
speaking.promptMn: Өөрчлөхийг хүсч буй зуршлынхаа тухай ярь: одоо юу хийдэг, яагаад өөрчлөхийг хүсэж байгаа, үүний тулд юу хийж байгаа вэ.
points: What you are doing about it (present continuous)
phrases: I have a bad habit of…
At the moment I'm trying to…
speaking.sample: I have a bad habit of checking my phone in bed. I usually read the news or watch videos for about an hour, so I go to sleep very late and feel exhausted in the morning. I want to break this habit because my sleep is really important for my work. At the moment I'm trying to leave my phone in the kitchen at night, and I'm reading a book instead. It's not easy, but I'm sleeping much better.
